chunks: And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, his brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who leaves his home intending another home of his or another estate of his, he said: 'If the distance between him and his home or the estate he intends is two burids, he shortens the prayer; and if it is less than that, he completes the prayer.'

key_terms.بَرِيدَانِ: Two burids, a unit of distance used in Islamic law to determine the threshold for travel prayers

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance required for a traveler to shorten their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the minimum distance threshold for the traveler’s prayer concession, defining 'two burids' (roughly 7-8 km) as the boundary between a resident and a traveler. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the ruling of qasr applies only when one intends to travel beyond this specific distance, ensuring that short prayers are not performed for mere local movements. This precise measurement underscores the juristic emphasis on intention and physical distance in determining religious obligations.
